notes: Saturn V leaves the pad at 13:32:00 UTC. Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins, and Buzz Aldrin are aboard for the Moon. Times in this file are UTC.
The third stage fires at 16:22:13 UTC and sends the crew out of Earth orbit toward the Moon.
The command module docks with the lunar module at 16:56:03 UTC and pulls it free of the spent stage.
The lunar-orbit insertion burn begins at 17:21:50 UTC. Apollo 11 is circling the Moon.
Armstrong and Aldrin undock the lunar module at 17:44 UTC. Collins stays in Columbia.
Touchdown at 20:17:39 UTC in the Sea of Tranquility. Armstrong: "The Eagle has landed."
Armstrong's boot meets the surface at 02:56:15 UTC. "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
Buzz Aldrin joins Armstrong on the surface at 03:15:16 UTC.
Armstrong reads the plaque at 03:24:40 UTC: "Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon."
The U.S. flag is deployed at 03:41:43 UTC.
Richard Nixon speaks with Armstrong and Aldrin from the White House at 03:48:30 UTC.
The hatch is closed at 05:11:13 UTC. Armstrong and Aldrin spent a little over two hours outside.
The ascent stage lifts off at 17:54:00 UTC to rendezvous with Collins.
Columbia and Eagle dock at 21:35 UTC. The lunar module is jettisoned later that night.
The transearth injection burn at 04:55:42 UTC puts Columbia on the long fall back to Earth.
Columbia hits the Pacific at 16:50:35 UTC, about 800 nautical miles southwest of Hawaii.
The crew, in biological isolation garments, reaches the recovery ship. President Nixon is waiting. They go straight into quarantine.
